title: Intervention verbs on a work item: requeue, retriage, cancel, close

story.as_a: Mark in fleet_dash, or any session that sees an item off course
story.i_want_to: re-queue, re-triage, cancel or close one work item with a reason
story.so_that: I can intervene anywhere, and a session can too, with every act recorded with its actor

rationale: PRD R4: 'Intervention verbs on the same API, open to fleet_dash and to sessions alike: re-queue, re-triage, move, cancel, close with a reason'. Today the only lever on an in-flight item is force_unclaim_story, which is exact_role: :orchestrator (story_verification_controller.ex:30-31), escalates the item over :operator_released (stages.ex:2013) and stays a custody gate, so fleet_dash's user key and a holder cannot take an item back to the queue at all; nothing cancels or closes an item, and re-triage exists only as a human resolution. PRD section 4 limits holders to one new edge out of escalated, escalated -> queued, so every verb that starts at escalated passes through queued over US-52.31's edge and continues from there.

acceptance_criteria.description: Loopctl.Delivery.Interventions.requeue/4 on an escalated item calls Escalations.resolve/3 with to: :queued (the edge chosen by the caller, US-52.31's rules); on an item at claimed, worktree, implementing, reviewing, pr_open or ci it releases the claim through Progress.force_unclaim_story/3 with release_cause: :intervention, which Stages.follow_release/5 settles at queued, uncounted, re-contracted, with the session dispatch revoked; any other stage is 409 not_requeueable naming the stage.

Interventions.retriage/4 on an item no implementer touched (Escalations' retriageable check) at escalated or queued moves it to detected over the new edge {:queued, :detected, :retriage}, passing through queued over the caller's resolution edge when escalated, clearing every identity triage_dispatch_id included and superseding its triage dispatches; an implementer-touched item is 409 not_retriageable naming what it holds.

Interventions.cancel/4 and close/4 move an item at detected, triaged, queued or an in-flight stage to failed (an escalated item through queued first, an in-flight item after an :intervention release), cancel over the new edge :cancelled whose resolution verdict is nil so the linked issue is left untouched, close over :closed whose verdict :not_actionable makes IssueCloser close the issue with the not-actionable label; an item at merged, deployed or verified is 409 already_landed for both.

The same commit adds to CLAUDE.md's Security & Trust Model checklist, after item 2 (CLAUDE.md:316), an intervention-verb carve-out stating that requeue, retriage, cancel and close are role: :agent behind RequireHumanAnchor because none reports, reviews, verifies or deletes, that a holder may not intervene on its own item, and that force_unclaim_story stays exact_role: :orchestrator; a doc test fails when the carve-out is missing or names a role other than the routes' own.

Each verb takes a required reason (1..4000 codepoints, sanitised as escalation reasons are) and a required intervention_id (UUID); it writes one 'intervention' event (verb, reason, actor_holder_id, actor_label, intervention_id) in the same transaction as its transitions; a retry with the same intervention_id returns 200 with the item's current stage row and writes nothing (unique index story_stage_events_intervention_uidx on (tenant_id, (data->>'intervention_id'))).

A holder may not intervene on an item whose stories.assigned_holder_id is its own holder_id (409 self_intervention_blocked; it escalates or unclaims instead); a non-human key with no holder_id is 409 holder_required; both refusals change nothing.

POST /api/v1/stories/:id/requeue, /retriage, /cancel and /close are role: :agent and RequireHumanAnchor, declare every refusal above in operation/2, and answer the item's stage row; another tenant's story is 404.

MCP tools work_item_requeue, work_item_retriage, work_item_cancel and work_item_close send reason and an intervention_id (generated when absent), have mcp-server/README.md rows and a wiring test; each description names what the verb refuses and that the linked issue is closed only by work_item_close.

test_cases.name: requeue from escalated, from in-flight, and refused elsewhere (DataCase)
preconditions: release 3 holder fixtures; items at escalated (by holder A), implementing (held by A under a session dispatch) and merged; holder B
expected_results: escalated -> queued over holder_resolution; implementing -> queued over claim_released with attempts unchanged, agent_status contracted, dispatch revoked; merged 409 not_requeueable

test_cases.name: retriage only for an untouched item, through queued (DataCase)
preconditions: an item escalated over :triage_escalate with triage_dispatch_id bound; an item escalated after implementing
steps: Interventions.retriage for both as holder B
expected_results: first at detected, triage_dispatch_id nil, transitions escalated->queued->detected; second 409 not_retriageable

test_cases.name: cancel leaves the issue open; close writes a not-actionable closure (DataCase)
preconditions: two queued items linked to intake records; an item at verified
expected_results: failed over cancelled with no closure; failed over closed with a :not_actionable pending closure; 409 already_landed

test_cases.name: an intervention retried with its id acts once (DataCase)

expected_results: both {:ok, row}; one intervention event, one transition

test_cases.name: a holder cannot intervene on its own item; a holderless key is refused (DataCase)
preconditions: an implementing item held by holder A; an orchestrator key with no holder_id
expected_results: 409 self_intervention_blocked and 409 holder_required, claim and stage unchanged

preconditions: holder B's agent key, a user key, a key of tenant B
steps: POST each verb with B's key

read the role on each of the four routes' plugs

technical_notes: Release causes: @release_causes (lib/loopctl/delivery/stages.ex:179) gains :intervention; settle/4 (:2013-2034) falls through to {:ok, {row, nil}} for it, so the row stays queued; the caller re-contracts through Stages.recontract_released/4 (:1836). force_unclaim_story/3 (lib/loopctl/progress.ex:4015) already forwards :release_cause (:4150); call the context function, never the exact_role: :orchestrator route, which stays a custody gate (PRD R4).

Edges: add {:queued, :detected, :retriage}, {from, :failed, :cancelled} and {from, :failed, :closed} for from in detected, triaged, queued to @transitions (stage_machine.ex:286); clears(:queued, :detected, :retriage) equals clears(:escalated, :detected, :human_resolution) (:957); @resolution_verdicts (:708) gains {from, :failed, :closed} => :not_actionable. All three are control-only: absent from runner_reportable_edges and refused by Stages.advance/4 from callers other than Interventions (the @release_only_edges pattern, stages.ex:2114).

An in-flight cancel or close first releases with :intervention (which lands at queued), then takes queued -> failed in the same transaction; an escalated item first takes US-52.31's edge to queued. Every verb is therefore one transaction under the story FOR UPDATE then stage row FOR UPDATE order (stages.ex:2569-2591).

Retriage reuses Escalations' retriageable/2 (lib/loopctl/delivery/escalations.ex:612) and DispatchLedger.supersede_triage_dispatches/2 (called at :524); make retriageable public as Escalations.retriageable?/2.

Closure: Stages.record_issue_closure/3 (stages.ex:981) writes the closure row when resolution_verdict/1 is non-nil, so close needs no closer code of its own; Loopctl.Delivery.IssueCloser (lib/loopctl/delivery/issue_closer.ex) performs it.

Intervention event and caller identity: the 'intervention' event kind, actor_holder_id and the api key's holder_id are provided by release 3 (README names table: work-item event log, holder credential). The partial unique index is new; name its migration after git fetch origin.

Who may act: role: :agent, the PRD R4 decision for intervention verbs. CLAUDE.md:316 keeps custody-critical work-breakdown operations at :user and calls an operation that serves as a custody gate :user-only; these verbs move an item's stage and claim but never report, review, verify or remove data, so AC-52.32.4 records them as a carve-out in the shape of the KB project-scope carve-out (CLAUDE.md:326). The self guard follows R4's 'a session never ... resolves its own escalation' to the item it holds.

Routes in lib/loopctl_web/router.ex beside /stories/:id/stage/resolve (:475), in a new LoopctlWeb.WorkItemInterventionController; MCP in lib/work-item.js (US-52.29) plus declarations and cases in mcp-server/index.js; CHANGELOG.md lists the new routes and edges.
non_goals: Moving an item to another holder or machine: release 7 (README names table: move verb).
The sweep that applies these verbs without a caller: US-52.34.

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.32.5: a client that loses the answer retries with the same intervention_id and gets the item's current row; nothing is applied twice.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.32.5: every intervention is an event row in the append-only log with its actor and reason, written in the same transaction as the transitions it caused.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.32.5: the intervention_id unique index makes a retried verb a no-op that answers the current row; TC-52.32.7 shows a verb racing the lease reclaim releases once.
failure_modes.slow: n/a: no network call inside the transaction; the issue close is IssueCloser's outbox work, performed later with its own bounded forge calls.
failure_modes.reach: n/a: runs inline in the request process; the only deferred work is the closure row IssueCloser drains.

definition_of_done: On production, work_item_requeue on an implementing story from a second session puts it at queued with agent_status contracted and story_stages.attempts unchanged.
work_item_close on a sandbox item closes its sandbox issue with the loopctl:resolution-not-actionable label.
git show of the story's commit touches CLAUDE.md's Security & Trust Model section and the intervention routes together.
defaults: close reports :not_actionable to the issue; cancel leaves the issue open with no comment.
An intervention release is uncounted: it does not spend an attempt against DISPATCH_MAX_ATTEMPTS.
The item's own holder may not intervene on it.
